title: Galois descent of closed subschemes and closed subgroups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $E/k$ be a finite Galois extension [def-pc-field-extension], meaning finite-dimensional, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal (each minimal polynomial of an element of $E$ splits in $E$), and let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X_E=X\times_k E$ [def-pc-base-change]. For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_k(E)$ write $\sigma_X=\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ for the induced semilinear automorphism. If a closed subscheme $Z_E\hookrightarrow X_E$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] is preserved as a closed subscheme by every $\sigma_X$, then there is a unique closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z\times_k E=Z_E$. If $X$ is a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] and $Z_E$ is a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], this descended $Z$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $X$.

source.place: Appendix A.65 (Galois descent for closed subschemes), printed pp.580–581, with A.66 (descent of morphisms) for the multiplication, inverse, and unit of a subgroup.

proof.text: For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify its inverse image with $U_E=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kE)$. By [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $Z_E\cap U_E$ has an ideal $J_U\subseteq A\otimes_kE$. Each $\sigma_X$ preserves $U_E$ and acts on its ring by $a\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes\sigma(c)$; this follows by evaluating on the two tensor inclusions. Since $\sigma_X^{-1}(U_E)=U_E$, [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] (with $g=\sigma_X$ and $V=U=U_E$) gives the ideal of the pulled-back closed subscheme $\sigma_X^{-1}(Z_E)$ on $U_E$ as the ideal generated by the image of $J_U$, which is that image itself since the ring map is an automorphism. Preservation as a closed subscheme therefore means that $J_U$ is stable under these maps, including when it is nonradical. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-stable-subspace-descent] with $M=A$, $L=E$ and $W=J_U$. Put $I_U=\{a\in A:a\otimes1\in J_U\}$. It is an ideal, since it is the inverse image of an ideal under a ring map. The cited lemma gives $J_U$ as the $E$-linear span of $I_U\otimes1$. This span equals the extended ideal $I_U(A\otimes_kE)$: multiplication of $a\otimes1$, $a\in I_U$, by $b\otimes c$ gives $(ba)\otimes c$, and pure tensors additively generate the tensor algebra.

source.place: A.64–A.65, printed pp.580–581, affine ideal descent; Stacks descent.tex Tag 0CDR (lemma-galois-descent) supplies the general linear descent framework.

proof.text: For $f\in A$, the principal open $U_f$ is affine with ring $A_f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](0). Under [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] the ring $(A\otimes_kE)_{f\otimes1}$ is $A_f\otimes_kE$, compatibly with restrictions. The ideal on $(U_f)_E$ is therefore $J_U(A_f\otimes_kE)$ by [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension] applied to this open restriction of the closed subscheme. Step 1 rewrites it as $(I_UA_f)(A_f\otimes_kE)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] the map $A_f\to A_f\otimes_kE$ is faithfully flat. Contracting this ideal gives $I_UA_f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]. By the definition in Step 1 that contraction is $I_{U_f}$. Hence $I_{U_f}=I_UA_f$ for every affine $U$ and $f$. This check uses principal opens inside each affine; it makes no assumption that intersections of arbitrary affine opens are affine.

source.place: A.65, printed p.581, passage from affine ideals to the closed subscheme; localization detail expanded using Stacks Tags 01QQ, 01IN, 05CK.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme](1) to the ideals $I_U$ and their principal-open compatibility from Step 2. It supplies a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ with ideal $I_U$ on every affine $U$. By [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension], its base change has ideal $I_U(A\otimes_kE)=J_U$ on every $U_E$. These opens cover $X_E$, by their description as inverse images in Step 1. Equality of the defining ideal sheaves (on each $U_E$ both are $\widetilde{J_U}$ by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]) gives, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic], a unique isomorphism over $X_E$, so $Z\times_kE=Z_E$, with the prescribed immersion. Here a closed subscheme is taken up to its unique isomorphism over its ambient scheme: locally its structure sheaf is the quotient by its ideal, as in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

source.place: A.65, printed p.581, construction by the descended defining ideals; Stacks 01QQ (lemma-closed-immersion-bijection-ideals) and 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme).

proof.text: Suppose another closed subscheme $Z'\subseteq X$ has the prescribed base change. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ let $I'_U$ be its defining ideal [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Its extended ideal is $J_U$ by [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension]. The map $A\to A\otimes_kE$ is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] gives $I'_U=\{a:a\otimes1\in J_U\}=I_U$. Thus the ideal sheaves and the quotient descriptions on every affine agree, giving $Z'=Z$ as closed subschemes by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic]. No reducedness is used.

source.place: A.65, first paragraph, printed p.581: uniqueness by contraction; Stacks algebra.tex 05CK.

proof.text: For a commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $x:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, we check that $x$ factors through $Z$ whenever its extension $x_E$ factors through $Z_E$. For an affine $U\subseteq X$ and $a\in I_U$, cover $x^{-1}(U)$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. On $V_E=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_kE)$, the restriction of $x_E$ kills the extended defining ideal, by Step 3 and [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension]. Hence the image $x^\sharp(a)|_V$ maps to zero in $B\otimes_kE$. It is zero in $B$, since [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat, lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] make $B\to B\otimes_kE$ injective. The sheaf axiom gives $x^\sharp(a)=0$ on $x^{-1}(U)$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections] supplies the factorization through $Z$. The converse follows by base changing a factorization. Thus membership in $Z(R)$ is reflected by extension to $R\otimes_kE$.

source.place: A.65–A.66, printed p.581, faithful detection of factorization through the descended closed subscheme; Stacks 05CK. This is the explicit ideal calculation for the subgroup deduction, without the separated-target graph method of A.66.

proof.text: Assume now that $X$ is a group scheme. For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, extend $R$ to the $E$-algebra $R_E=R\otimes_kE$. The base-change universal property identifies $X_E(R_E)$ with $X(R_E)$ and $Z_E(R_E)$ with $Z(R_E)$, compatibly with products, inverse and identity [def-pc-base-change, def-sc-group-scheme]. The hypothesis [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] says that $Z_E(R_E)$ is a subgroup of $X_E(R_E)$. The identity of $X(R)$ therefore extends to a point of $Z_E(R_E)$; so do the product of any two points of $Z(R)$ and the inverse of any such point. Step 5 puts each of them in $Z(R)$. Finally $Z(R)\to X(R)$ is injective: two lifts of a point agree locally over every affine chart of $X$, since maps through $A\twoheadrightarrow A/I_U$ are uniquely determined by their composites with this surjection [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. They agree globally by the sheaf axiom. Consequently $Z(R)\subseteq X(R)$ is a subgroup for every $R$, which is exactly the closed subgroup condition [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. This includes nonreduced test algebras.
